decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper+Houndoom to set rain via Drizzle and immediately pressure the opponent's biggest threat (Mega Gengar) with Dark Pulse. Pelipper's Hydro Pump 4x hits Aerodactyl through Focus Sash in rain, and its U-turn pivots into back. Houndoom's Flash Fire absorbs Arcanine Fire switches. Back: Blastoise Megas and Water Spouts in rain for the sweep; Snorlax is immune to Shadow Ball (safe Gengar switch-in), Thick Fat walls physical attackers, and provides a Curse win condition if rain ends.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag, Gengarite, Timid 143-178/165-200 mega), Aerodactyl (Wide Guard, Focus Sash, Jolly 165-200 spe), Arcanine (Intimidate, Extreme Speed, Lum, Jolly 126-161 spe), Dragonite (Life Orb, Inner Focus, Adamant 100-132 spe), Empoleon (Water/Steel, Competitive, Sitrus, Modest 80-112 spe), Hydrapple (Grass/Dragon, Regenerator, Leftovers, Modest 64-96 spe). Key threats: Mega Gengar Shadow Tag (traps after Mega), Aerodactyl Wide Guard (blocks Water Spout spread), Arcanine Intimidate+ESpeed (weakens phys, has priority). Rain core (Pelipper+Blastoise) is the win condition but vulnerable to Wide Guard. Houndoom is the Gengar check: Dark Pulse SE, Flash Fire absorbs Arcanine Fire. Blastoise must Mega to access Water Spout. Snorlax immune to Shadow Ball, Thick Fat handles Ice/Fire. Plan: Set rain T1, pressure Gengar with Houndoom Dark Pulse, break Aerodactyl sash with Hydro Pump, pivot with Pelipper U-turn into Blastoise sweep, Snorlax Curse as backup if rain ends or Gengar KOs a threat.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar-Mega. Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl outspeed the entire opposing roster. Turn one Wide Guard neutralizes Water Spout and Earthquake spread spam while Gengar Mega Evolves to trap targets and OHKO Pelipper with Thunderbolt. Empoleon and Hydrapple complete the plan with quad-resistances to water in rain, Competitive pressure against Tauros Intimidate, and unmatched durability against Snorlax and Toxapex.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Mega Blastoise, Pelipper (Drizzle), Houndoom, Snorlax, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead outspeeds entire opposing roster. Wide Guard blocks Water Spout / EQ; Shadow Tag traps key water/rain targets for Thunderbolt KO. Empoleon + Hydrapple backline quad-resists Rain attacks and punishes Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Split offensive pressure T1. Pelipper Hydro Pump hits Aerodactyl 2x SE in rain STAB — single-target so Wide Guard cannot block it, breaks the Focus Sash and chunks Aero. Houndoom Dark Pulse hits Gengar 2x SE with Life Orb, forcing Gengar into Protect or eating ~60%+. If Gengar Megas, Shadow Ball on Houndoom is NVE 0.5x and Houndoom lives; Houndoom outspeeds un-Mega Gengar and chunks back. Keeps Pelipper healthy for future pivot into Blastoise Water Spout after Aero is softened/sashed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team confirmed: Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag, Gengarite, Timid), Aerodactyl (Wide Guard, Focus Sash, Jolly), Arcanine (Intimidate+ESpeed, Lum, Jolly), Dragonite (Life Orb, Inner Focus, Adamant), Empoleon (Competitive, Sitrus, Modest), Hydrapple (Regenerator, Leftovers, Modest). Rain core is the wincon — Pelipper Drizzle + Blastoise-Mega Water Spout. Wide Guard on Aerodactyl is the main counter; Houndoom Dark Pulse keeps Gengar honest (SE 2x). Snorlax Thick Fat handles Arcanine/Empoleon Ice-Fire. Plan: T1 break Aero sash and pressure Gengar; T2 pivot Pelipper U-turn into Blastoise-Mega for Water Spout under rain; Snorlax as Curse/rest backup if rain ends or Gengar lands a trap.

decisions.rationale: Pivot Blastoise in. Confirmed Water Spout is neutral (1x) into Gengar-Mega (not resisted). Damage range 66.5-148.1% = likely OHKO in rain with Mega Launcher boost. Blastoise-Mega's 120/115 defenses eat Shadow Ball (28-57%) without falling. Turn 3 Mega Evo + Water Spout ends Gengar. Aerodactyl will pivot out (1% sash gone), opening rain sweep. Snorlax is too passive — Body Slam immune on Gengar, no wincon progress.
decisions.notebook: Confirmed: Water Spout neutral (1x) vs Mega Gengar — was wrong about Poison resist. Range 66-148% means probable OHKO at full HP in rain. T2 plan: switch Blastoise in, eat Shadow Ball. T3: Mega Evo + Water Spout for Gengar KO. Aerodactyl pivots out (no sash), likely to Arcanine or Dragonite. Rain up 4 more turns post-T2. Snorlax backup plan if rain dies: Curse + Rest stall, Thick Fat handles Arcanine/Empoleon. Watch for Arcanine Intimidate on switch — irrelevant to Blastoise SpA but matters for physical switch-ins. Opponent team: Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag), Aerodactyl (WGuard/Tailwind/Taunt), Arcanine (Intimidate+ESpeed Lum), Dragonite (Inner Focus LO Adamant), Empoleon (Competitive Sitrus Modest), Hydrapple (Regenerator Leftovers Modest). Wide Guard only on Aerodactyl — gone after pivot. Tailwind from Aero is the main speed threat to manage with rain turns.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom's Life Orb Dark Pulse threatens an immediate OHKO on Gengar. Protecting Gengar on turn 1 allows it to safely Mega Evolve into Shadow Tag without taking a super-effective attack. Aerodactyl uses Rock Slide to deal 54-114% damage to Houndoom and break Focus Sashes/chip Pelipper, setting up a guaranteed trapped turn 2 win position.

Pelipper Hydro Pump on Gengar (71-140% in rain, neutral) + Blastoise Water Spout spread (67-131% on Gengar, 0.75x) = combined 138-271% = guaranteed OHKO Gengar (no-Protect path). Also KOs 1HP Aerodactyl via WS spread hit. No-mega preserves SpA 150 and mega for T3. If Gengar Protects (1/3), T2 wasted but T3 Water Spout no-mega gives 49% OHKO. Removes Shadow Tag T2.
decisions.notebook: Confirmed: Water Spout is allAdjacentFoes (does NOT hit Pelipper ally, verified). Water Spout vs Gengar in rain: 67-131.9% (49% OHKO on hit, 0.75x spread). Pelipper HP vs Gengar in rain: 71.3-140% (neutral, water on Ghost/Poison = 1x). T2 exec: Pelipper HP Gengar (80% acc) + Blastoise WS spread (no mega). Combined 138-271% on Gengar = guaranteed OHKO. KOs 1HP Aero too. Preserve mega for T3. Gengar Protect (1/3): T2 wasted; T3 no-mega Water Spout 49% OHKO. Mega Launcher: 1.5x boost to Dark Pulse. Mega evolution drops SpA 150→135 (bad for Water Spout, good only for Dark Pulse). Rain timer: 4 turns. Use water moves aggressively. Aerodactyl pivots: Arcanine (Intimidate NVE to my special attackers) or Dragonite (ESpeed priority threat). After Gengar: focus pivot target, watch ESpeed. Empoleon weak to water spam in rain. Snorlax backup plan if rain dies: Curse+Rest stall, Thick Fat handles Arcanine/Empoleon.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Both Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) and Aerodactyl (200 Spe) outspeed the entire opposing side (Blastoise max 130, Pelipper max 117). Aerodactyl's Rock Slide deals 44-50% to 50% HP Pelipper to finish it off while chipping Blastoise. Gengar's Thunderbolt onto Blastoise deals 48.9-87%, giving a strong chance to double KO this turn. Even if Blastoise survives, its HP drop severely neuters Water Spout's Base Power.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Mega Blastoise, Pelipper (Drizzle), Houndoom, Snorlax, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Both Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl (200 Speed) outspeed Blastoise and Pelipper. Wide Guard nullifies Water Spout.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega (200 Speed) outspeeds Blastoise (max 130) and easily KOs its 15% HP next turn. Hydrapple is the safer switch-in over Empoleon because it resists Ground (Earthquake from Tauros/Snorlax) and Water in Rain, whereas Empoleon is weak to Fighting (Close Combat) and Ground.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Mega Blastoise (Water Spout, Dark Pulse, Ice Beam, Protect), Pelipper (Drizzle, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, U-turn, Protect), Houndoom (Life Orb, Fire Blast, Dark Pulse, Sludge Bomb, Protect). Remaining options in back: Snorlax, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Shadow Tag locks non-Ghost grounded foes.

decisions.rationale: Mega Dark Pulse targets the immediate faster threat and is the strongest listed hit into Gengar; Body Slam pressures Hydrapple without harming Blastoise. This covers Gengar Protect by damaging Hydrapple and avoids Earthquake finishing our 15% Blastoise.
decisions.notebook: Confirmed: Water Spout is allAdjacentFoes and does not hit ally. Gengar commonly protects early, then targets Blastoise with Thunderbolt. Aerodactyl used Rock Slide twice and did not establish Tailwind. Preserve Snorlax as the rain-expiry endgame; Curse plus Rest is the fallback, with Thick Fat useful into Arcanine and Empoleon. Blastoise is the intended Mega; Mega Launcher boosts Dark Pulse, while Mega evolution lowers its Special Attack from 150 to 135, so avoid Mega for Water Spout/Ice Beam unless strategically necessary. Against Hydrapple, Blastoise is guaranteed faster before priority and Ice Beam is the listed 4x attack. Focus Gengar first when exposed, then use Ice Beam pressure into Hydrapple; watch Dragonite and Arcanine Extreme Speed on low-health targets.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega (200 Speed) outspeeds Blastoise (max 130 Speed) and guarantees a KO with Thunderbolt on 15% HP before Blastoise can attack. Even if Blastoise Protects, Snorlax's max physical threat (Earthquake) deals 59.6-88.2% damage, which Gengar-Mega (91% HP) easily survives. Fickle Beam offers Hydrapple's highest STAB power into Snorlax.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team preview brought: Mega Blastoise, Pelipper, Houndoom, Snorlax. Non-brought: Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Shadow Tag traps grounded non-Ghost foes.

decisions.rationale: Snorlax is the endgame sweeper; Curse boosts Atk/Def and pairs with Thick Fat to wall future Arcanine/Empoleon. Body Slam into Gengar is immune; into Hydrapple risks Spore-less para but Gengar outspeeds and threatens Psychic SE next turn if Snorlax is locked on a less-than-ideal target. Curse is safe — only Gengar threatens Snorlax (immune Ghost, Psychic SE), and Gengar likely protects or doubles. Earthquake hits ally Blastoise (already dead next hit) but still wrong. Rest only if low. Curse now
decisions.notebook: Rain 2 turns left. Aerodactyl, Pelipper, Houndoom, Blastoise-Mega fainted. Remaining: Snorlax. Foe remaining: Gengar-Mega, Hydrapple in; Dragonite, Empoleon, Arcanine in back. Foe items: Gengarite, Leftovers(Hydrapple), LifeOrb(Dragonite), Sitrus(Empoleon), Lum(Arcanine). Gengar commonly protects, then TBolt into Water. Aerodactyl never set Tailwind. Snorlax is rain-expiry sweeper: Curse up, pivot Body Slam for para chip, Rest as fallback. Thick Fat walls Arcanine FlareBlitz and Empoleon Ice Beam. Plan: Curse this turn, threaten Gengar with Body Slam next turn if it stays, sweep weakened back once Gengar falls.

decisions.rationale: Snorlax is the opponent's final remaining Pokémon. Gengar (Speed 200) and Hydrapple (Speed 64) both outspeed Snorlax (Speed 50-82). Psychic and Fickle Beam deal heavy special damage that ignores any Curse Defense boosts. Unboosted Earthquake caps at 88.9% against Gengar, so Gengar survives at 91% HP and secures the KO this turn or next.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 1 roster revealed: Mega Blastoise, Pelipper, Houndoom, Snorlax. Non-brought: Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Shadow Tag traps grounded non-Ghost foes.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily due to a flawed team-preview plan against this opponent. The chosen core (Pelipper + Blastoise-Mega + Houndoom + Snorlax) was hard-countered: Gengar-Mega outspeeds Blastoise-Mega and one-shots it with super-effective Thunderbolt in rain, Aerodactyl's Rock Slide hit both Pelipper and Houndoom super effectively on turn 1 (instantly removing Houndoom and chunking Pelipper), and Snorlax never got a safe turn to set up Curse before being chipped by Hydrapple's Fickle Beam and finished
reflections.adjustment: Reconsider the four brought and the Mega. Against a Gengar-Mega + Aerodactyl lead, do not lead Houndoom + Pelipper (Rock Slide deletes both). Lead Snorlax + Pelipper instead: Snorlax's Thick Fat and natural bulk absorb Rock Slide and Psychic while Pelipper sets rain, giving Snorlax safe Curse turns. Either drop Blastoise-Mega entirely (it cannot touch Gengar and folds to TBolt) or pair it with a dedicated Gengar answer (e.g., a Ground- or Dark-resistant pivot) and Protect it turn 1. If keeping B
reflections.notebook: Opponent durable tendencies: leads Gengar-Mega + Aerodactyl; Gengar commonly Protects turn 1 then clicks TBolt/Shadow Ball into the Water-type; Aerodactyl pressures with Rock Slide (did not set Tailwind game 1 — may use it game 2 if I give it a turn); Hydrapple is the cleanup mon, uses Fickle Beam aggressively and pairs with Regenerator to pivot in safely. Revealed strategic facts: opponent's team is built to dismantle rain — Gengar-Mega TBolt deletes rain cores, Aerodactyl Rock Slide chunks Flying/Water/Fire leads, Hydrapple walls Snorlax with Fickle Beam. Foe items confirmed: Gengarite, Focus Sash (Aerodactyl, consumed), Leftovers (Hydrapple), Life Orb (Dragonite), Sitrus (Empoleon), Lum (Arcanine). Future plans: avoid Houndoom + Pelipper lead vs this squad; prefer Snorlax + Pelipper to set Curse in rain; do not bring Blastoise-Mega without a Gengar check; watch for Aerodactyl Tailwind on turn 1 if I give it space; keep Snorlax away from Hydrapple until Gengar is down; Arcanine (Intimidate + Lum) and Empoleon (Sitrus) in back are the late-game walls — Snorlax Body Slam para + Curse boost is the path through them.

reflections.summary: The Mega Gengar plus Aerodactyl lead directly exploited opponent's vulnerable Pelipper/Houndoom opening, using superior Speed, fast Rock Slide pressure, and Gengar's Thunderbolt coverage under Shadow Tag to dismantle their core before Snorlax could set up.
reflections.adjustment: Anticipate opponent leading Tauros-Paldea-Blaze or Toxapex in Game 2 to absorb Rock Slide and check Gengar; position Empoleon or leverage Gengar's Psychic early to punish Intimidate or defensive pivots.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega (Water Spout), Pelipper (Drizzle/Hydro Pump), Houndoom (Life Orb), Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate), Toxapex (Kasib Berry/Haze/TSpikes). Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead heavily pressures their rain/fire core via fast Rock Slide and Thunderbolt coverage. Shadow Tag prevents Pelipper/Blastoise switches.
